ai_show_review.summary: Stellar China>Rider, Uncle John's Band and rich Garcia steel
ai_show_review.blurb: The show shines with a fiery China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue, tight High Time energy and standout Uncle John’s Band into Black Peter. Jerry’s pedal‑steel on the opening trio and his fluid lead guitar are highlights, while Phil adds solid bass and vocal depth.
ai_show_review.review: On February 7, 1970 at San Francisco’s Fillmore West the Dead delivered a set that balances country‑flavored experimentation with their emerging electric groove. The night opens with an unexpected pedal‑steel showcase on “Saw Mill,” giving Garcia a chance to shine on a instrument rarely heard in the band’s catalog. From there the group rolls into a classic “China Cat Sunflower” → “I Know You Rider” transition that reviewers call “fiery” and “effortless,” highlighting Jerry’s soaring lead lines. Mid‑set momentum builds through “High Time” and “Green Green Grass Of Home,” before the band settles into a heartfelt rendition of “Uncle John’s Band,” featuring Phil’s distinct vocal contribution, which then flows seamlessly into the melancholy “Black Peter.” The second half, while described by some as less inspired, still offers solid musicianship and a crisp drum foundation from Mickey and Billy. Overall, the performance captures the Dead at a pivotal moment—still rooted in their acoustic past yet pushing forward with the improvisational fire that would define the ’70s.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard source with crisp, well‑balanced mix that captures the pedal‑steel intro and Garcia’s lead tones clearly, minimal hiss and no major dropouts.

key_highlights: Fiery China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider segue with blazing improvisation
Uncle John's Band into Black Peter delivering tight vocal harmonies and emotional depth
Jerry's pedal‑steel opening trio on Saw Mill adds a unique country flavor
High Time and Green Green Grass Of Home showcase the band's mid‑set groove

band_performance.Jerry: Pedal‑steel on the opening trio is a unique treat; his lead guitar throughout is effortless, rich and full‑tone, with solos that hint at new possibilities.
band_performance.Phil: Provides distinct vocals on Uncle John's Band and lays down solid bass support, though early mix can sound boomy before settling.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are steady and present, providing a reliable backbone without any standout issues.
band_performance.Billy: Drums are steady and present, providing a reliable backbone without any standout issues.
